 Advertisement Subtropical storm could develop in the Atlantic this week
 After two quiet weeks, the Atlantic has a new area to watch. If it forms, it would take the name Subtropical Storm Kyle.
 By Miriam Guthrie and Rob Shackelford • just now Updated: November 5, 2026, 5:25 am EST Published: November 5, 2026, 5:25 am EST Share Share
 1 . The latest Chevron Down Watching an area in Atlantic for subtropical development
 A subtropical storm could form in the Atlantic this week, after two weeks without activity in the basin. 
 If it develops, it would take the next name in the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season list, Kyle.
 The latest
 It may be November, and it may have been quiet since Subtropical Storm Josephine, but we have an area to watch for development in the Atlantic Basin.
 Weather in your inbox Forecast Location Sign Up By signing up you agree to the Terms & Privacy Policy . Unsubscribe at any time. A broad area of low pressure is located well off the East Coast and a few hundred miles to the south of Bermuda. 
 If that area of low pressure pops enough thunderstorms near its center, it could transition into something called a subtropical storm. 
 (WATCH: Rising surf from Josephine cuts off homes on Outer Banks )

 But this storm’s window is somewhat tight. It has to get its act together by this weekend, because if it doesn’t, unfavorable conditions will end its chances of getting a name by early next week, according to the National Hurricane Center.
 Fortunately, it will remain far off the East Coast, and poses no threat to the U.S. 
 But it could bring some impacts to Bermuda, including high surf and breaking waves, and eventually some increase in winds and rain showers.
 Regardless of what meteorologists call it, this system is expected to drift to the east or northeast into the open Atlantic Ocean. 
 What is a subtropical storm?
 On Oct. 21-22, Subtropical Storm Josephine briefly formed off the East Coast, and this system has the chance to become Subtropical Storm Kyle. 
 A subtropical storm is a type of storm that is a mix between a tropical storm and the kind of low pressure system you see on weather maps attached to cold and warm fronts. 
 (MORE: What is a subtropical storm? ) 
 The National Hurricane Center issues advisories and forecasts for subtropical depressions and storms and they are assigned a number or name, just like a tropical depression or storm.
 Subtropical storms can still bring heavy rain, gusty winds and storm surge like a tropical system or hurricane.
